shouldFix: Decision 9 references 'the selected read-only EWMH/root probe' without committing to a specific command. The design offers wmctrl -m or xprop -root _NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK as alternatives but leaves the choice open. Test-plan should pin the exact command and define its success/failure criteria deterministically so can_query_windows has unambiguous test coverage.

Decision 1 states that new machine-readable details do not overload checks[*].detail prose, but the design does not enumerate what new check entries, if any, are added to the checks[] array alongside the new fact sections. The spec minimum is 'at least one self-check or doctor-internal check entry,' which the existing bootstrap already satisfies. Test-plan should explicitly enumerate the expected checks[] entries in the expanded report to prevent silent drift.

Decision 5 defines SourceOverlayFacts with notes: Vec<String> and screenshot_provider_mapping: Vec<String>, and Decision 11 mentions that the later tasks.md must carry forward acceptance criteria, but neither decision specifies whether those Vec<String> fields are static compile-time strings reflecting spec acceptance records or runtime-derived values. This distinction affects what assertions are meaningful in tests. The test-plan should clarify which fields are static-populated and which are runtime-derived before writing fixture tests for source_overlay.
summary: The design artifact is internally consistent and aligns well with the proposal, specs, grill resolutions, and project constraints. All proposal-stage obligations and specs-stage obligations are addressed. Secret safety is handled explicitly. No upstream-required fields are invented. The additive report model, blocker-based readiness, strict portal parsing, ydotool socket candidate ordering, and source-overlay acceptance plan are all coherently specified. Three minor implementation-detail gaps are noted as shouldFix items appropriate for clarification at test-plan/tasks stage rather than blocking this stage.
